object_context: First strict spectral/lattice-RG atom for the Yang–Mills Millennium program: identify the exact quantitative obligations needed to transport a finite-lattice transfer-matrix or Euclidean correlation gap into a nonzero finite physical mass gap for the continuum four-dimensional quantum Yang–Mills theory, uniformly in the thermodynamic limit and along an asymptotically-free continuum scaling trajectory, without conflating confinement/area-law information, stochastic-dynamics gaps, lattice-unit decay, and the full physical spectrum.
structural_coordinates: The Clay root requires a nontrivial quantum Yang–Mills theory on R^4 for every compact simple gauge group, with axioms at least as strong as the cited Wightman/Osterwalder–Schrader framework and a finite positive mass gap above the vacuum.

A reflection-positive Euclidean lattice formulation can yield a positive self-adjoint transfer matrix, but transfer-matrix existence alone supplies no uniform spectral lower bound and no continuum construction.

If a one-time-step transfer matrix is normalized as T_a = exp(-a H_a), then the physical excitation energy associated with eigenvalue ratio lambda_1/lambda_0 is -a^{-1} log(lambda_1/lambda_0); the exact normalization and domain must be witnessed for the chosen lattice construction.
A finite physical continuum gap m_*>0 corresponds to a lattice-time decay exponent of order a m_* as a->0, not to an a-independent lower bound on the dimensionless one-step exponent.
Thermodynamic volume L->infinity and continuum cutoff a->0 are distinct limits; any usable estimate must state its quantifiers, limit order or joint regime, and uniformity.
Strong-coupling lattice theorems control fixed-cutoff regimes far from the weak bare-coupling asymptotically-free continuum trajectory unless a rigorous RG/coarse-graining bridge is proved.
Ultraviolet RG control at weak bare coupling is structurally complementary to, but does not itself imply, an infrared mass gap.

Wilson-loop area law and suppression of center-flux sectors constrain extended or center-sensitive observables; a Clay-scale mass-gap conclusion requires control of the full gauge-invariant physical spectrum or a source family proved complete enough to detect every low-energy excitation.

A stochastic/Langevin generator Poincare or log-Sobolev spectral gap is not automatically the Hamiltonian/transfer-matrix mass gap; any implication must be proved through the exact Euclidean observable and reconstruction framework.
Numerical glueball spectra and Monte Carlo correlation lengths are calibration/falsification evidence only under RAKL and cannot substitute for proof or continuum construction.
equivalent_formulations: After OS/Wightman reconstruction, prove Spec(H) is contained in {0} union [Delta,infinity) for some finite Delta>0, with the vacuum at energy zero.

Along a lattice scaling trajectory a->0 and L->infinity, prove -a^{-1} log(lambda_1(a,L)/lambda_0(a,L)) >= Delta_* > 0 with the correct transfer-matrix normalization, together with the convergence/reconstruction hypotheses needed to identify the limiting spectrum.
Prove exponential clustering in physical distance for a gauge-invariant local observable family that is demonstrated to have spectral overlap sufficient to exclude every excitation below Delta_*.

Control the physical correlation length xi_phys(a,L)=a xi_latt(a,L) uniformly from above along the continuum trajectory, while separately proving that the lattice measures/Schwinger functions converge to the required nontrivial continuum QFT.

Construct an RG transport statement that connects weak-bare-coupling ultraviolet control to a scale where a rigorous infrared correlation/spectral estimate applies, preserving reflection positivity/locality and a quantitatively trackable physical gap.
solved_analogues: Osterwalder–Seiler 1978: reflection positivity/physical positivity for lattice gauge approximations implies a positive self-adjoint transfer matrix; at strong coupling they also establish an infinite-volume lattice regime and a Wilson confinement bound.

Shen–Zhu–Zhu 2023: in explicit strong-coupling regimes for lattice SU(N)/SO(N) Yang–Mills, functional inequalities yield infinite-volume uniqueness and exponential decay of correlations for a broad observable class at fixed lattice cutoff.
near_solved_analogues: Balaban 1987 and related RG work: four-dimensional pure lattice gauge theory admits rigorous weak-coupling/small-field renormalization-group control and coupling-constant renormalization, but this does not close the nonperturbative infrared mass-gap bridge.

Cao–Nissim–Sheffield 2025: expanded rigorous Wilson-loop area-law regimes provide a modern confinement-side calibration, but area law is not by itself a theorem about the entire neutral transfer-matrix spectrum.

explicit_disanalogies: A positive spectral gap for Langevin dynamics is not the quantum Hamiltonian mass gap without an explicit bridge.
Exponential decay in lattice units at fixed strong coupling is not a continuum physical gap unless its rate scales and survives correctly as a->0.
An a-independent lower bound on the dimensionless one-step transfer exponent is not the desired finite physical mass statement; with T_a=exp(-aH_a) it would correspond to energy growing like 1/a.
Wilson area law or center-sector suppression does not automatically exclude low-energy center-neutral states.
Ultraviolet asymptotic-freedom/RG control and infrared strong-coupling mass generation occupy different regimes until a quantitative transport theorem connects them.
Numerical agreement of glueball masses across lattice spacings is not a proof of continuum existence, spectral completeness, or a uniform lower bound.

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A topological code can strongly suppress global logical-flux errors while local syndrome correlations and the excitation spectrum carry different information; decoding success therefore does not certify a complete local spectral gap.
common_abstraction: global topological/extended-sector control and local excitation-spectrum control are distinct
a measured family of observables may miss a hidden low-energy sector unless it is proved spectrally complete
coarse-grained effective descriptions require stability and scale-transport obligations
source_to_target_mapping: logical/topological flux sector -> center-flux / Wilson-loop confinement sector
local syndrome/source correlator -> gauge-invariant Euclidean source correlator
hidden logical/excitation sector -> possible low-energy physical state with weak or zero overlap with the tested source
code coarse-graining/stability -> RG/coarse-graining of lattice gauge theory
shared_constraints: sector suppression and local spectral exclusion must not be conflated
source completeness must be proved if a correlation family is used to infer a full gap
scale transport must preserve the property being certified
disanalogies: the code setting has finite/discrete logical structure whereas non-Abelian continuum Yang–Mills has an infinite-dimensional physical Hilbert space
the 2026 source is a proposal/preprint and does not furnish a Clay-scale theorem
a decoding threshold and a relativistic QFT mass gap have different mathematical definitions
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Before using confinement or decay of a selected observable family as a mass-gap surrogate, isolate a spectral-completeness obligation: every physical state below the proposed gap must have nonzero overlap with at least one controlled gauge-invariant source.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: In the exact reflection-positive lattice transfer-matrix framework, either prove that the controlled source algebra is cyclic/dense enough to detect every candidate sub-gap physical excitation, or exhibit a model/counterexample showing that the confinement/decay criterion can coexist with an undetected low-energy sector.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Structural proposal inspired by Ning Bao, arXiv:2608.02452 (2026); used only as a cross-domain analogy and warning, never as theorem authority.
